title: Multiomics Profiling of HERV Modulation and Immune Activation via RIG-I and IFNAR Pathways in Human Airway Epithelial Cells
projectDescription: Comprehensive multiomics analysis to investigate host cell responses upon immune system activation in human non-tumoral airway epithelial cells (BEAS-2B). Transcriptome and proteome profiling were integrated to capture global gene and protein expression changes, together with the modulation of Human Endogenous Retroviruses (HERVs), focusing on two distinct immune activation checkpoints: RIG-I and downstream IFNAR interferon receptors.
sampleProcessingProtocol: BEAS-2B cells were lysed in HEPES-based buffer and sonicated. Proteins (50 µg per sample) were reduced with TCEP and alkylated with CAA, then digested overnight at 37°C using LysC and Trypsin via S-Trap column. Peptides (10 µg) were labelled with TMTpro 18-plex reagents (Thermo Scientific) at 2.5:1 reagent:peptide ratio across 12 channels. Pooled samples were fractionated by HPLC into 24 fractions and loaded (400 ng/fraction) onto an Orbitrap Ascend coupled to a Vanquish Neo nanoHPLC system with a 90-minute gradient.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw proteomic data were processed using Proteome Discoverer 2.4 (Thermo Fisher Scientific). MS2 spectra were searched against the human reference proteome (UniProt/SwissProt, April 2024) plus common contaminants (244 entries) using SequestHT, with precursor mass tolerance of 7 ppm and fragment mass tolerance of 0.5 Da. Static modifications included carbamidomethylation on cysteines and TMTpro labelling on N-termini and lysines; oxidation on methionines was set as dynamic modification. FDR was controlled with Percolator (< 1% at PSM level). Protein quantification required PSMs with signal-to-noise > 10, ≥ 50% SPS matches, and unique peptides > 2; only high-confidence proteins (q-value < 0.01) were retained. Statistical analysis was performed with MSStatsTMT (R, v1.8.2) using PSM-level input, spectrum normalization, and linear mixed-effects models (padj ≤ 0.01, |log2FC| ≥ 1). Transcriptomics and proteomics data were integrated using OmnipathR and biomartr; enrichment analysis was performed with enrichR (v3.2).
